evals.prompt: Implement the plan at .claude/plan/jwt-auth.md — it adds JWT authentication with refresh tokens to the Express API.
evals.expected_output: Claude reads the plan, implements the changes, calls codex-call.sh for review with structured verdict prompt, fixes accepted findings at every severity until a clean round, and delivers a summary table.
expectations: Claude reads the plan file before implementing (Read tool called on .claude/plan/jwt-auth.md)
Claude uses Edit or Write tools to modify production files
Claude calls codex-call.sh (not `codex review`) for the review phase
The Codex prompt includes 'VERDICT: APPROVED | WARNING | BLOCKED' format
The Codex prompt includes 'Be concise'
Claude outputs a delivery table with File, Operation, and Description columns
Claude reports the Codex review result (clean after N rounds, or UNREVIEWED) in delivery

evals.prompt: Add input validation to the registration endpoint — validate email format, password strength, and username length.
evals.expected_output: Claude implements directly (inline task, no plan file), calls Codex for review, and delivers.
expectations: Claude does NOT attempt to read a plan file (uses task description directly)
Claude calls codex-call.sh for review after implementation
The Codex prompt includes 'git diff HEAD' instruction

If Codex returns any accepted finding at any severity (BLOCKED, WARNING or MEDIUM/LOW under APPROVED), Claude fixes every accepted finding and re-reviews; there is no WARNING proceed-without-review path
Delivery includes a changes table and review result

evals.prompt: Add a caching layer to the user service, session service, product service, order service, and notification service.
evals.expected_output: Claude dispatches subagents for the 5+ tasks (3+ threshold) rather than implementing inline, then calls Codex for review.
expectations: Claude identifies this as 3+ implementation tasks and dispatches Task subagents
Claude records git SHA before each subagent dispatch (git rev-parse HEAD)
Claude runs git diff after each subagent to verify changes
Claude runs scoped lint/tests after each subagent completes
Claude calls codex-call.sh for review after all subagents complete
Claude does NOT use Bash codex review command

evals.prompt: Add a health check endpoint to the API server.
evals.expected_output: Claude detects that Codex (codex-call.sh or the CLI) is not available and stops with a clear error message — does NOT proceed without review.
expectations: Claude runs the codex-call.sh availability check before Phase 3
Claude stops and tells the user that Codex CLI or codex-call.sh is not available
Claude mentions that this skill requires Codex for review
Claude does NOT deliver a completion table without Codex review
Claude does NOT fall back to a non-Codex review — it fails closed

evals.prompt: [claude-codex] Review loop stress case: the reviewer still lists one accepted HIGH finding in rounds 1 through 6 and returns a clean round in round 7.
evals.expected_output: Claude fixes and re-reviews every round, continues into round 6 and round 7, and delivers only after the clean round.
expectations: Claude starts a 6th review round instead of stopping after 3 or 5 rounds
Claude never asks the user whether to keep going because of the round count
Delivery reports a clean final round and zero remaining findings

evals.prompt: [claude-codex] The first review round returns VERDICT: APPROVED with CRITICAL none, HIGH none, MEDIUM none and LOW: one accepted naming issue.
evals.expected_output: Claude treats the LOW-only round like any other round with findings: fixes it and re-reviews.
expectations: Claude fixes the LOW finding instead of delivering or asking the user
Claude runs another review round after the fix
The same handling applies to a round with only HIGH or only MEDIUM findings

evals.prompt: [claude-codex] The review call times out, and the single retry also returns no VERDICT line.
evals.expected_output: Claude labels the work UNREVIEWED and never reports it as approved.
expectations: Claude retries the failed review exactly once
Claude tells the user the work is UNREVIEWED
Claude does not describe the work as approved or reviewed
